notes: T1656 Impersonation and T1672 Email Spoofing are revoked in ATT&CK 20.x and replaced by T1684.001 and T1684.002 (Social Engineering); the current IDs are used here.
ATT&CK 20.x renamed the Defense Evasion tactic; these techniques are under Stealth.

techniques.name: Proxy: Multi-hop Proxy
techniques.description: Routing traffic through several proxies such as Tor to hide its source; here: sending via an anonymising exit.

techniques.name: User Execution: Malicious Link
techniques.description: Relies on the recipient clicking a malicious link; execution itself is not observable in an email.

techniques.name: User Execution: Malicious File
techniques.description: Relies on the recipient opening a malicious file; execution itself is not observable in an email.

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.description: Malicious file attached to an email to gain initial access when the recipient opens it.

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Link
techniques.description: Email containing a link to an attacker-controlled or malicious resource to gain initial access.

techniques.name: Acquire Infrastructure: Domains
techniques.description: Registering or acquiring domains, e.g. look-alike domains used for sending or hosting links.

techniques.name: Establish Accounts: Email Accounts
techniques.description: Creating new email accounts (often free or look-alike) to send messages or receive replies.

techniques.name: Compromise Accounts: Email Accounts
techniques.description: Using an existing, legitimate email account that has been taken over to send messages.

techniques.name: Phishing for Information
techniques.description: Messages that try to make the recipient reveal credentials or other information, e.g. by replying.

techniques.name: Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Link
techniques.description: Messages with a link intended to collect credentials or other information (e.g. a fake login page).

techniques.name: Financial Theft
techniques.description: Stealing money or other monetary resources, e.g. by redirecting a payment in business email compromise.

techniques.name: Social Engineering: Impersonation
techniques.description: Posing as a trusted person or organisation (executive, colleague, supplier) to persuade the target to act.

techniques.name: Social Engineering: Email Spoofing
techniques.description: Forging sender-identity header values (e.g. From) so a message appears to come from someone else.
